page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Why false fruits
lines: A true fruit develops only from the ovary.
Fruits that develop from any other floral
part - such as the thalamus or the pedicel -
steps.why: The definition is a contrast with the true fruit: ovary = true; any other part (thalamus, pedicel) = false.
common_mistakes: Writing that false fruits form without fertilisation. That is parthenocarpy - a different idea.
steps.memory_tip: True from the ovary; false from anything else.
steps.margin_note: State the true-fruit line first - the contrast is the reason asked for.

steps.label: Two examples

lines.text: Apple: the fleshy thalamus forms the fruit.

steps.why: Each example should name the non-ovary part that grew - thalamus in apple, pedicel in cashew - which proves the definition.
common_mistakes: Listing banana. Banana is parthenocarpic, not false - it still comes from the ovary.
steps.memory_tip: Apple from the thalamus, cashew from the stalk.
steps.margin_note: Example + its floral part; the part is what earns the mark.
